newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Luz del Sur to invest $170 mln over 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Luz del Sur to invest $170 mln over 5 yrs.

text.p: The Peruvian electricity utility Luz del Sur, which will see up to 30 percent of its state-held shares sold next month, plans to invest $170 million over the next five years, an official said Monday.
The investment is aimed principally at expanding the distributor's service to supply more customers, said company spokesman Carlos Spa.
The government, which hopes to raise $200 million in total from the privatization, plans to start the sale on November 18 with the offer of shares to Peruvian nationals.

Officials from CS First Boston - the investment bank chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the offer - have said they expect the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
Privatization officials have not announced the date for the start of the international offer but expect to set the price for the placement on December 6.
The government holds a 30 percent stake in the electricity company but has not formally specified what proportion of its shares it will sell.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
